home.faqSub: Everything you need to know before you search.
home.faq1a: We search airlines and travel agents to find the best flight options. We don't charge booking fees — you book directly with the provider at their price.
home.faq2q: How can I find the cheapest flight?
home.faq2a: Search flexible dates and try the trip finder or the price map to explore the lowest-cost destinations. Mid-week departures and booking 3–8 weeks ahead usually surface the best fares on short-haul routes.
home.faq3q: Do I book my flight with TicketsJet?
home.faq3a: No. TicketsJet is strictly a search engine. You complete the booking directly with the airline or travel agent on their own platform, at the exact price shown.
home.faq4a: Flights and car rentals are our focus. For hotels, our Stays search opens Booking.com in a new tab, where you compare and book. TicketsJet doesn't compare hotel prices yet.
home.faq5a: We compare leading rental companies for competitive prices, free cancellation options and fair full-to-full fuel policies.
home.faq6a: Your confirmation email comes directly from the airline or provider you booked with. For changes or support, contact them directly — they hold your reservation.

flights.tipsTitle: How to pay less for the same seat
flights.tip1d: Tuesday and Wednesday departures are routinely 15–25% cheaper than Friday and Sunday on the same route.
flights.tip2d: Let fares pick your destination. Searching a whole country or a flexible month surfaces deals you would miss city by city.
flights.tip3d: 3–8 weeks ahead for short-haul, 2–5 months for long-haul. Last-minute bargains are rare on popular routes.
flights.playbook: Want the full playbook? Read our guide:
flights.playbookLink: How to find cheap flights in 2026
flights.faq1q: When is the cheapest time to book a flight?
flights.faq1a: For short-haul routes, the best fares usually appear 3–8 weeks before departure. For long-haul, aim for 2–5 months out. Tuesday and Wednesday departures are consistently the cheapest days to fly.
flights.faq2a: Yes — the strip of nearby dates under your search shows fares around your departure day, and the trip finder compares a whole month.
flights.faq3a: Prices shown come from airlines and agencies. The final price is confirmed on the provider's own site during checkout, before you pay.
flights.faq4q: Can I book flexible or refundable tickets?
flights.faq4a: Many airlines offer tickets with free date changes. Apply the flexible-ticket filter in your search results to see only those fares.

lon.name: London
lon.blurb: Europe's busiest city break, with five airports and dozens of daily flights from most hubs.

par.name: Paris
par.blurb: Short, frequent flights make Paris one of the easiest weekend trips in Europe.

bcn.name: Barcelona
bcn.blurb: Beach, architecture and food in one city, served by both full-service and low-cost airlines.

rom.name: Rome
rom.blurb: Flights reach Fiumicino and Ciampino; low-cost carriers often fly to Ciampino.

mad.name: Madrid
mad.blurb: A major hub for flights onward to Latin America as well as a destination in its own right.

ist.name: Istanbul
ist.blurb: Straddles two continents, with two main airports and many direct routes from Europe and the Gulf.

dxb.name: Dubai
dxb.blurb: A global transit hub with long-haul routes in every direction.

cai.name: Cairo
cai.blurb: Direct flights from many European and Gulf cities; popular year-round.

ruh.name: Riyadh
ruh.blurb: The capital's King Khalid airport is well connected to Europe, Asia and the Gulf.

jed.name: Jeddah
jed.blurb: Gateway to Makkah and the Red Sea coast, with busy seasonal demand.

cmn.name: Casablanca
cmn.blurb: Morocco's main hub, with many direct flights from Europe.

nyc.name: New York
nyc.blurb: Flights serve JFK, Newark and LaGuardia — compare all three in one search.

bkk.name: Bangkok
bkk.blurb: A common first stop for travel across Southeast Asia.

mnl.name: Manila
mnl.blurb: Long-haul routes usually include one stop; compare duration as well as price.

ams.name: Amsterdam
ams.blurb: Schiphol is one of Europe's largest hubs, with excellent connections.

dub.name: Dublin
dub.blurb: Frequent short flights from the UK and continental Europe.

lis.name: Lisbon
lis.blurb: A compact capital with direct flights from most major European cities.

ath.name: Athens
ath.blurb: Gateway to the Greek islands; summer schedules add many extra routes.

vie.name: Vienna
vie.blurb: Well served by full-service carriers from across Europe.

fra.name: Frankfurt
fra.blurb: A major connecting hub, often the cheapest way to reach long-haul destinations.

london.blurb: Museums, royal palaces, gardens and river views. Many of the big sights have timed entry, so booking ahead saves queueing.
london.tip1: Many major museums are free to enter, but special exhibitions are ticketed.
london.tip2: A single-day pass often beats buying each ticket separately if you plan three or more sights.

paris.blurb: Art, architecture and river cruises. The Louvre, Eiffel Tower and Versailles all work best with a pre-booked time slot.
paris.tip1: Book the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre ahead; same-day slots often run out.
paris.tip2: Versailles is a half-day trip from the centre, so plan it separately.

rome.blurb: Ancient sites, the Vatican and plenty of food stops. Combined tickets cover the Colosseum, Forum and Palatine Hill.
rome.tip1: The Colosseum, Forum and Palatine are usually sold together.
rome.tip2: Vatican entry is timed, and security queues can be long in peak season.

barcelona.blurb: Gaudí's buildings, beaches and tapas. The most popular interiors have limited daily entry.
barcelona.tip1: Sagrada Família and Park Güell need a booked time slot.
barcelona.tip2: Group your Gaudí sights by area to save travel time.

amsterdam.blurb: Canals, world-class museums and cycling. Popular museums and canal cruises are worth booking in advance.
amsterdam.tip1: The Rijksmuseum, Van Gogh Museum and Anne Frank House use timed tickets.
amsterdam.tip2: Public transport passes can cover the city and the region.

madrid.blurb: The Prado, royal palaces and lively evenings. Madrid also makes a good base for day trips to Toledo and Segovia.
madrid.tip1: The Prado, Reina Sofía and Thyssen are close together on the Paseo del Prado.
madrid.tip2: Many day-trip tours leave from the city centre in the morning.

istanbul.blurb: Mosques, bazaars and Bosphorus cruises across two continents. Guided tours help with the old city's layered history.
istanbul.tip1: Dress modestly when visiting mosques; some close briefly for prayer times.
istanbul.tip2: A Bosphorus cruise is a relaxed way to see both shores.

lisbon.blurb: Hilltop viewpoints, historic trams and day trips to Sintra. Plan for hills and comfortable shoes.
lisbon.tip1: Sintra is easy by train, but its palaces have their own entry queues.
lisbon.tip2: Tram 28 gets very crowded; go early or choose another route.
